messages:
Sam: Quick async standup — sprint ticker
Sam: Done: landed kernel microqueue change that short-circuits empty-batch slots, added a lag-limiter to reduce tail amplification.
Sam: Measured with local driver: p50 ~12ms, p95 jumped to ~240ms on a few burst traces.
Sam: Blocker: one benchmark run showed a weird spike when seq_len=512 + batching_factor=8, need help reproducing on canary because my rig is noisier than infra.
Sam: Today: triage the p95 spike, run a controlled canary on staging, open a small follow-up PR to tighten backoff.
Anya: @Sam can you paste the exact bench command you ran? I can kick off a repeat on our staging sharers.
Sam: sure —
Sam: ```bash
# run harness with fixed seed and workload mix
python infra/bench/run.py --model gpt-small --seq 512 --batch 8 --seed 42 --trace out/trace-512b.json
```
Sam: and the quick log excerpt:
Sam: ```
[2026-03-17 09:12:03] INFO batcher: slot_acquire latency=11ms
[2026-03-17 09:12:07] WARN kernel: microqueue overflow, draining=4
[2026-03-17 09:12:08] INFO kernel: generate p95=243ms p99=512ms
```
Kevin: fwiw I saw similar spikes when the cache warmup hits a shard boundary. Did you have KV cache enabled?
Sam: yes KV cache ON, prefix caching enabled. I suspect the lag-limiter + cache eviction interacts badly when a hot prefix crosses a shard migration.
Anya: I'll run that exact command on staging-3 with KV shard alignment toggled. If it's a shard boundary, we should see the spike only when alignment=false.
Beth: @Sam tagging: does this change affect Dedicated pools? We should check rollout policy before we push to prod.
Sam: good call — the change is opt-in behind feature flag kernel.microqueue.short_circuit. Default is off for Dedicated. I'll open the PR with the flag and a rollout note.
Sam: PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8241 (requesting review from @Kevin and @Beth)
Kevin: I'll take the review after Anya's canary run. If she reproduces, prioritize adding a guard to disable the lag-limiter on shard-boundary detection.
Anya: started a run on staging-3 now, estimate 25m. I'll post the trace and raw numbers here when done.
deploy-bot: Canary deployment started: canary-2026-03-17-kernel-microqueue on staging-3 (3/10 hosts)
Sam: thanks. tiny follow-up: when you look at traces, check for contiguous slot_hold times >50ms — that's the pattern I was seeing.
Beth: noted. Also worth adding a short README section in the PR about how to interpret the trace fields for non-obvious metrics (slot_hold, drain_count, prefetch_delays).
Sam: will do.
Kevin: unless the canary reproduces, seems low-risk. If it does reproduce we ship a revert-slash-hotfix today.
Sam: cool. If nobody objects I'll queue the PR for review after Anya posts results.
Anya: quick update: reproduced, attaching summary in 10m.
Sam: ack, thanks all :thumbsup:
